validation_notes: The right side of the chart shows price consolidating in a tight, roughly flat range (~0.0405-0.0440) after a sharp downtrend from late July. There's no clear rising support line - lows are essentially flat/choppy rather than making higher lows, and highs are also flat rather than descending in a converging manner. This looks more like a flat consolidation/range-bound base after a downtrend than a descending triangle. A descending triangle requires clear lower highs converging into a flat support; here both boundaries appear roughly horizontal and parallel, which resembles a rectangle/range rather than a converging triangle. Volume spike mid-range (Aug 1) also disrupts clean pattern formation. Insufficient evidence of trendline convergence to confidently call this a triangle.
